content.comment_body: Hello, I'm looking for some advice. I have an older [product_name] ([article_no]) that I want to use for a GSM alarm. I need help getting the outputs to switch in specific sequences, for example: I1 goes high, then: Q1 four times Q2 five times Q1 once Q2 once Q1 once Q2 twice Q1 five times Q3 once Is it possible to accomplish this? I've thought about using an old mobile phone to send SMS messages at different alarm inputs. The mobile connections are set up, but I'm struggling to program the [product_name]. Has anyone done something similar or have any ideas on how to begin? /[user_name]

You can configure [product_name] software by using CTRL+H (Select Hardware) to set it to the [article_no] version. Then create your program. However, your sequence might be too large for a [article_no], but it would fit easily on a [article_no] with more memory.

Thank you, I know it's possible to change to other hardware models in the software. What I need help with is identifying which function blocks are necessary for the feature I'm aiming for. If it doesn't fit the [article_no], I do have alternatives. I don't want someone to build the whole program for me—I just need pointers on how to start. /[user_name]
I had some spare time, so I created a sample program for you. It works with the [product_name] [article_no] or newer versions. No thanks needed.

Thanks for that, I really didn't expect someone to make it for me. I'm used to trying on my own, but when I can't figure things out, I ask for help to get started. Thanks again—I'll look at it tomorrow since it's getting late. /[user_name]

Hello, now that things have settled after the Christmas weekend, I tested the program and it worked well. However, there was no reset, so the alarm couldn't restart automatically. I added a reset myself. I ended up creating my own version so it would function on the [article_no]. //[user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers around configuring an older [product_name] ([article_no]) for complex GSM alarm output patterns.
